Volatility Analysis & Regime Detection

Regime method: daily log returns are converted into 63-trading-day realized volatility and classified by empirical sample thresholds: Low ≤ 13.6%, Normal ≤ 17.2%, High ≤ 24.3%, and Crisis > 24.3%. This percentile-based approach avoids externally imposed thresholds and keeps the classification dataset-native.

Seasonal & Calendar-Based Patterns

Monthly effect size: η² = 0.0014. This is the share of return variance explained by calendar month; values near zero imply weak practical seasonality even when individual months look different.
Day-of-week effect size: η² = 0.0005. The chart uses annualized daily means for comparability, but statistical interpretation should focus on t-statistics and p-values.

Daily return autocorrelation is -0.016 at 1 trading day and -0.022 at 21 trading days, indicating that momentum should be evaluated through trend filters rather than raw daily serial correlation. The correlation between absolute daily returns and log volume is 0.085, while the correlation between intraday range and log volume is 0.362. Because early volume observations are frequently zero, post-2003 average volume (4,766) is a more representative liquidity baseline than the full-sample mean.

Key Takeaways & Forward-Looking Considerations

  • Portfolio role: full-sample CAGR of 12.38% with volatility of 17.69% produces a Sharpe-like ratio of 0.70, supporting gold as a macro allocation whose value depends on regime timing and drawdown tolerance.
  • Risk management: maximum drawdown of -44.36% and excess kurtosis of 7.02 show that sizing should be governed by tail-risk constraints, not only by average volatility.
  • Regime monitoring: the latest observation is classified as Crisis with 63-day realized volatility of 36.5%; movement above 24.3% would place gold in the dataset-defined crisis-volatility band.
  • Seasonality: month and day-of-week effect sizes are small (η² 0.0014 and 0.0005), so calendar effects are better treated as weak overlays rather than standalone allocation signals.
  • Liquidity caution: volume metrics before 2004 are structurally unreliable due to zero/very-low entries; liquidity conclusions should emphasize the post-2003 subsample.
